title: The Return of M
text: “Filolial Cross!”
The queen cheers on that Trash like an idol fan. You can kind of tell she’s captivated by him.
“Mother… Hey, Naofumi… Is it really okay if I run away from home?”
“You have a mansion in the town next to ours, don’t you? Why don’t you take refuge there? You can just stay with Filo for a while.”
“I’ll take you up on that… Filo-tan is my source of comfort right now…”
Finacée’s eyes are dead. Filo-tan really is an angel, after all!
“Well then, I’m counting on you from now on! Together, we’ll lead the world to peace!”

And so, with Trash as their leader, Ren, Itsuki, Fleon-chan, Black Thunder, and the others returned, and they resumed their various activities across the land. The world of Ogi-butan, where Rival went… Ah, since Fleon-chan said Ogi-butan is a respectable person, I understood he isn’t actually a pig.

It was Glass, wasn’t it? Apparently, he’s been traveling back and forth between that world and this one, moving around extensively and living a fulfilling life. By the way, it seems Glass’s companions are there as well.

The rest of this update is based on stories I heard from my Father and Rival. I hear Ren’s companions were also dragged along by the Divine Bird Knights to another world, where they’ve been engaged in all sorts of activities. Apparently, they’re wondering why they’re doing this, but they say that going on various adventures alongside Ren, whom they respect, hasn’t been a bad experience.
As for Leiska, she’s still making a racket as usual. Her movements have improved, though, and it seems she’s grown enough to be chosen as a throwing weapon confiscated from Takt.

And so, the turmoil came to an end, and life shifted to days spent handling the aftermath of the war—hunting down reincarnated beings and quelling the conflicts breaking out in various regions. The Sage listened with great delight to Fleon-chan’s tales of her adventures in the other world. Yuki-chan competed in the Filolial Race she’d long dreamed of and easily snatched the victory.

Of course, she also competed in the Filolial Queen & King Cup. Although Yuki-chan had already given birth and retired in her first world, she fought valiantly and snatched the victory. It seems Fleon-chan and Filo-tan find flying more enjoyable than running fast. It’s just a matter of personal preference.
As for Yuki-chan, even after winning, she hasn’t let it go to her head and continues to practice. She often races against me. I still can’t let Yuki-chan beat me!
And then… one day, the carriage began to rattle and shake. Today, I’m on a leisurely peddling trip with my Father and the others.
“Naofumi, you really like peddling, don’t you?”
“Rafu.”
My Father is accompanied by my Big Sister, the Rafu, as well as Filo-tan, my Finacée, Rival, and Tiger Guy. Glass seems to be searching for something in that other world, so he went back.
“If we stayed in the village, we’d get dragged into trouble with that noisy Justice Squad Knight Corps. Taking it easy like this while peddling is the best way to go.”
“That’s true. That’s why I’m tagging along, too.”
“I don’t know about those guys, but they even got introduced to a hidden dungeon in this world and went ahead and cleared it. Was it the Prado Desert?”
“I gave them a few hints, thinking it might buy us some time, but they cleared it way faster than I expected. Awakened Trash—he’s next-level.”

Apparently, Rival introduced that machine from the Prado Desert to the Divine Bird Knights, led by Trash. Things were quiet for a while, but they’ve returned after completing the dungeon. The famine caused by the tidal wave damage has been completely resolved. Rival said there’s a similar place in that world too, so he told them to head over there.
“Those guys are way too well-organized for no reason.”
“I guess so… They’re not doing anything wrong—in fact, it’s a good deed, so I can’t really complain.”

“The Filolial Cross-led Knight Order takes down the overt enemies, the Bow Hero faction handles the hidden enemies, and the Sword Hero faction deals with lone perpetrators… Seriously, they’re way too well-organized for no reason.”
“And then there’s the one who bridges the different senses of justice between Itsuki’s followers and Ren’s followers… Filolial Cross! Right…? It’s like, ‘Give me a break.’”

Apparently, most people tend to get along well with one of these three factions or another. “The orthodox faction, the underground organization, and the lone wolves,” as my Father used to say. It seems Filolial Cross acts as a mediator between those with differing ideologies.

“Over in that world, while they were preparing for war, during a small gathering, some Trash without a mask—acting all cocky and flashing a contemptuous smile—said, ‘The formations ordered by those reincarnated folks are all just the same old, mindless “encircle and annihilate” tactics.’”
“Ah… I kind of get what kind of formation that is.”

Time to show off my history knowledge, huh? Believe it or not, history is actually my strong suit. When it comes to encirclement and annihilation, General Hannibal’s Battle of Cannae is famous, isn’t it? It’s such a well-known strategy that I’ve even seen it used in manga from my world.

According to history, it’s said to be a highly effective strategy, but the standard tactics must be different in this other world. After all, in this world where Magic exists, if you form a formation so tightly packed that you can be surrounded, you’ll just become easy prey for Magic. If it were me, I’d either hurl a “Prominence” at a clustered enemy or use a sweeping “Brionac” to wipe out even a scattered formation in one fell swoop. Also, we mustn’t forget that the Battle of Cannae—famous for this encirclement and annihilation tactic—took place in the pre-Christian era.

Even aside from the Battle of Cannae, this tactic has been used throughout history in many different eras and locations. It’s such a standard strategy that it’s even featured in military treatises in this world—it’s that common. The world isn’t so forgiving that you can outsmart it with a tactic like this.

“Encircling the enemy is a struggle in itself, and there are countless other issues—terrain, reinforcements, and so on. You said it requires a lot of conditions to work. Besides, there’s always the possibility of attacks from outside the range—like with large-scale area-of-effect magic—so you can’t rely too heavily on any single strategy.”

“Well… since it’s the kind of thing found in military strategy manuals, there’s probably a standard playbook for breaking through it, and with magic involved, there’s bound to be even more variation…”

“Of course. At the same time, ‘I see. Now I understand why this formation was used so often in past wars in my world, even if it seemed pointless. This must be what it means to be a reincarnated warrior. When they fail, only their one-man-against-a-thousand feats get recorded.” I found myself nodding in agreement.”

In other words, even if they fail, they can still defeat the enemy by brute-forcing their way through using the special abilities unique to reincarnated warriors, and the operation is deemed a success. It’s become a bit of a mystery how a failure can still be considered a success. Incidentally, while there have been reincarnated warriors who lost battles in history, it seems they’re still remembered because they employed similar strategies.
"Ah, come to think of it, I hear the first World Takt used this formation as well."

Apparently, it was deployed in operations other than aerial bombardments by aircraft. Either way, it seems they were all wiped out before that Trash operation could even begin. Incidentally, Takt was defeated by my Father from the separate unit.

“When a small group of reincarnated warriors charged in, the Filolial Cross just snapped their fingers and said, ‘Isn’t this what you wanted to do?’ Then they surrounded them as a group and annihilated them. If it works well, it’s definitely awesome.”

“From Trash’s perspective, reincarnated warriors seem like easy targets… He can beat them just based on raw strength, and he’s got strategy and charisma to spare… If Trash and I were to face off, I’d definitely lose on strategy alone. Well, I don’t really come up with strategies to begin with, though.”

My father has a deep understanding of those matters… Basically, he leaves it all to the experts. Still, among the Four Holy Heroes, my father is probably the best at command. That’s beyond question. However, since he’s a Hero, it would be a mistake to rely solely on Father’s command—especially since he has to fight on the front lines. We absolutely need someone other than Father to oversee the overall command.

After all, as the Shield Hero, Father is, by nature, positioned at the very front, so he simply doesn’t have the bandwidth to command the entire army. His role is more like a squad leader or a military commander than a general. He’s the squad leader in charge of commanding my Big Sister and Filo-tan, after all.
“That Trash really knows how to use the terrain. Just look at how many enemies he’s taken down with terrain-based traps… It’s no wonder Siltvelt had such a hard time.”
“Is it really that bad…?”
“Come to think of it, he used the floating rocks from the Graweik ore to neutralize the airplanes, didn’t he?”
That was during the operation in the first world. The airplanes were charging in, getting battered, and crashing to the ground.
“That’s why I sometimes find myself almost swept up by something like that… I wonder if that’s what they call my father’s charisma at his peak.”
“Hey, if even Melty ends up on that side, I’ll be in serious trouble.”
“It would be easier if that happened… but I’m being forced to do Merphilo, aren’t I?”
“Ah, that.”
“The other day, I did Merphilo at a fairly large venue… and it was there.”
What was there, exactly? I have absolutely no idea.
“My mom, in disguise… She was waving one of those Merphilo merchandise wands sold by Gaelion and cheering me on…”
“Your mom really is such a bandwagon fan, isn’t she…”
Finacée’s eyes are truly vacant.
“‘Go for it! Merphilo!’—what do you think of the sight of your own mother shouting that, Naofumi?”
“It made me want to die.”
“Yeah… so I guess I’ll never end up on that side, then…”
“That’s a relief. I’ve got to stay as far away from those guys as possible.”
“That said, Filolial Cross is handling the political stuff pretty well, isn’t it?”
“Hey… speaking of Filolial Cross… whenever something comes up, they try to hand me that Iron Mask…”
Tiger Guy says to his Father and the others with a troubled expression.
“They probably want to make you their successor. Like, have you step into the spotlight as a Trash and keep maintaining peace with Filolial Cross.”
“Please stop… I can’t handle politics. I trust Atla because she says I’m like her, but I can’t pull off something like that…”

“I’ll admit he’s impressive, though… I guess the Trash takes a liking to you. Probably because he sees himself in you… You know how it goes? If you put on that mask and say something like, ‘Filolial Cross has received that will!’ maybe Trash will be satisfied and retire.”
“Don’t just leave me hanging like that…”
“But still, putting on a mask like that…”
“Do you have a complaint against Filolial-sama?”
Trash has finally come to understand Filolial-sama.
“There’s no doubt it’s a suspicious creature. At the very least, it’s not just a creature that carries luggage. It’s something else—something that transcends monsters.”
“What is it, then? I’ll take you on if you want a fight!”

“Motoyasu, calm down. This is all your fault—yours, Fleon’s, and Black Thunder’s. We also have to do something about the infection problem among the village’s Filolials. Melty and Filo, make sure to keep a close eye on them.”
“It’s a bit less stressful than dealing with my father and the others… though it’s actually tougher than when I’m trying my best to ‘ride out the storm.’”

By the way, no campaigns have been launched against the Pig King of Faubrey or anything like that. I don’t know if that’s considered a necessary evil, or if they just don’t think it’s time to take action yet. According to my Father, overthrowing Faubrey would be an excessive act of justice for them, right? Isn’t that based on his experiences during the revolutionary unrest when Itsuki went into hiding? That’s the theory, anyway. Well, it’s certainly a hassle. I suppose Ren, Itsuki, Fleon-chan, Black Thunder, and the others won’t go poking around in the underbrush unnecessarily.
“I’m pulling Filo’s work carriage!”

Oh… Filo-tan is in a good mood. I’m tagging along with Yuki-chan and Kou. After all, I want to protect my father and Filo-tan. And the place we ended up at was… oh… it brings back memories. It was the town where I confirmed I’d been tricked by the Crimson Swine—the town where Ren and the Crimson Swine escaped through a portal only to be caught by my father.
As dusk began to fall, my father and the others—who didn’t feel like returning to the village via portal—decided to stay the night here. I’m joining them, too.
Ah… everything here brings back memories. This is the tavern where I first met Filo-tan. I step inside and sit down, lost in thought, on the chair where I used to sit.
“Motoyasu-sama! Dinner is ready!”
“Indeed. It’s different from the food that Father makes, but this is actually a pretty decent tavern. After all, it’s the tavern where I made my memories.”
“That’s right!　I’m sure the food here will make my legs feel lighter. And I should calculate the nutritional value of the meal… Hmm.”
Yuki-chan still seems to love running as much as ever.
“Come on, Raphtalia.”
“Naofumi-sama, please don’t try to naturally lift me onto your lap. I’m not a Beastman, you know?”
“Is that a no?”
“It’s a no.”
“I see… Well then, I’ll just have Raph-chan sit with me this time.”
“Sigh… I’m tired of having to keep reminding you, so fine.”
With a deep sigh, Big Sister sat down in the chair next to Father and ordered some food.
“Naofumi, I think it’s about time you just accepted Raph as she is.”
“You’re right…”
“I’m being honest, you know.”
“How should I put it… All the heroes seem to have gone a little crazy. Naofumi is no exception.”
"I actually think Naofumi is a decent person. As Gaelion, I know a much kinder side of Naofumi."
"I get that there are glimpses of it here and there… but it’s like all of that is concentrated in Ms. Raphtalia…"

Over there, a little ways away, your Finacée is deep in conversation with a Rival. If she keeps talking to a dragon like that, Filo-tan will get angry! I’d really prefer if she stopped! Filo-tan! Jealousy is no good! Or so I thought—but when I looked over at Filo-tan, she was happily singing in the tavern. Ah… that sight is exactly the same as the Filo-tan I remember. Filo-tan’s singing is a big hit—the tavern patrons are cheering her on. My Finacée even joined in, singing and dancing, and time slipped by in a lively whirlwind. Filo-tan and the others received all sorts of gifts from the patrons. Then, carrying a mountain of presents, Filo-tan made her way over to me.
“What’s wrong, Uruwashu? Did something bad happen?”
Ah… this scene is exactly the same as the Filo-tan in my memories.
“When I get hungry, you see, I lose my energy, don’t I? I’ll sing you a song to cheer you up.”

Filo-tan is singing for me, just as she did in my memories, looking exactly the same. Oh… that’s right, Motoyasu—the love you hold comes from Filo-tan. No matter what kind of Filo-tan she may be, you must not be afraid. After she finished singing, Filo-tan gave me some vegetables and flowers from the gifts she’d brought.
“Eat this, cheer up, and ask me for more ‘Uruwashu’ meals again, okay?”
she said, beaming from ear to ear. Suddenly… I felt a sense of clarity, as if all my previous fears had been swept away.
“H-hey. Spear Hero. I can tell you’re feeling better now, so calm down. We’re in such a nice spot—you’ve got to hold it in, got it? You understand? Calm down.”
My Rival is saying something, but I couldn’t care less.
“What? Is something wrong?”
“Hurry up and subdue the Spear Hero! Otherwise, it won’t be good for the Spear Hero!”
My rival is ordering Tiger Guy while trying to fly over here.
“U-uh, waaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaah!”
I lunged at Filo-tan.
“Nyaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaaa!?”
“Filo-chan!? Spear Hero, calm down a bit, will you?”
“Ugh… Just when we’d finally built a good relationship and were so close to the finish line… I blew it.”
My Rival is muttering something with a “Oh, well” kind of look, but I couldn’t care less! And just like that, I finally overcame my fear of Filo-tan and won back her love!

That’s right!

And so, I pulled myself together, and my love for Filo-tan grew even stronger than before. I went on drives with Filo-tan all over the place in Drive Mode. I even had a rendezvous in the sky with Filo-tan in Flying Mode as she soared away! We’ll be together forever!
Selective Retrospection
Send Sakura-chan to her Finacée.
Give preferential treatment to Tiger Girl.

I won’t give up!
Random Rewind ←
Eighth Coordinate… Reference… Verification… Rewind Initiated—
“Filo, you know. I want to see the same thing that Master—who sometimes stares off into the distance—and big sister Raphtalia and the others are looking at. Hey, how can Filo get to that same place?”
“Hmm… that’s quite difficult, isn’t it? You’d need to be fully prepared and determined never to look back… no matter how many goodbyes you have to say, could you really live without any regrets?”
“Oh?”
Suddenly realizing something, I look around. There’s my Father, Ren, and Itsuki. Where is this, I wonder? It looks vaguely familiar…
“Huh? The wave arrival time suddenly disappeared…?”
My Father said this as if he’d just noticed something unusual. Judging by his tone of voice and the way he treats Ren and Itsuki, he’s a kind Father. It seems we’ve looped again.

And when I turn my attention to the people other than Ren and Itsuki… there’s Big Sister’s older sister and the Panda. And then there’s Éclair, Sakura-chan, Kou… and Yuki-chan. Yuki-chan isn’t an adult—she’s a child.
“Motoyasu-kun, do you have any idea what’s going on?”

I’ll have to check a few things. This place… is, if I’m not mistaken, where we fight the reincarnated warriors of the final wave. A loop where I went to such a place with my kind Fathers… well, in the case of my Father who sacrificed himself to the Rival, that wouldn’t be right since Itsuki is dead. But Itsuki is here. So that probably means…
“W-what…? What’s going on?!”
Just then, the Rival let out a cry next to the Assistant, as if suddenly snapping back to reality.
“Gaelion, I’ve looped back!”
“Huh?”
Father turned his gaze toward Rival.
“Didn’t Gaelion just say she’d looped back?”
The Assistant said, looking at Rival.
“That’s right! This place is… yeah. There’s no mistake. Spear Hero, this must be the loop where you led the heroes to Faubrey!”
The 'Legendary Filolial Arc' has concluded. Starting next chapter, we will transition to the Faubrey & Zeltoble Arc: Part 1 - After the Four Cardinal Heroes Arc.
